```{r a2-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.6,
  fig.height = 4.8, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%")
options(width = 82)
```

School accountability tables often rank schools by their observed chronic
absence rates, placing every pair of schools in order even when small
enrollments or nearby rates leave their comparison uncertain. Here we use
California chronic-absenteeism data to walk through a one-criterion grading
that places schools in ordered integer grades and leaves within-grade pairs
unordered.

The target quantity is each school's current chronic-absence probability `p`,
oriented as $\theta = -p$ so lower absence receives higher priority (grade 1).
This descriptive target measures current school absence rates in the source
frame; it does not estimate a school's causal effect on attendance or
reproduce the California School Dashboard's two-dimensional Status-plus-Change
color rules.

All posterior inputs and optimization results below are stored in the package
and loaded without fitting a model or running a solver during rendering.

## Schools, counts, and empirical-Bayes posterior {#start-with-schools-counts-and-a-posterior}

The case study comes from the 2026 California School Dashboard
chronic-absenteeism release (academic year 2025--26). Its statewide frame
covers `5,834` non-alternative (non-DASS) elementary-type schools (including
eligible charter schools) with usable all-student counts and denominators
`n >= 30`. Because the denominator is each school's indicator-eligible student
count, summing denominators across schools need not equal a count of unique
students.

`pr_case_cde` holds a 12-school teaching subset selected deterministically
from `4` observed-rate rank groups crossed with `3` denominator rank groups
(one school per cell). That selection spans rate and enrollment strata for
illustration; it is not a representative sample for estimating statewide
chronic absence.

Source data come from the
[CDE chronic-absenteeism download collection](https://www.cde.ca.gov/ta/ac/cm/chronicdatafiles.asp);
source conditions are posted at the
[CDE copyright statement](https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp). Only the
12 selected school IDs and counts and author-derived posterior summaries are
bundled here; no Creative Commons or MIT code license is substituted for the
CDE source conditions, and no CDE endorsement is implied (see `?pr_case_cde`
and the installed `DATA-NOTICE.md`).

```{r a2-input}
library(postrank)
case <- pr_case_cde
input <- case$input
schools <- case$units

school_labels <- setNames(paste("School", LETTERS[seq_len(nrow(schools))]),
  schools[["entity_id"]])
criterion_labels <- setNames("Lower chronic absence (-p)", input[["criterion_ids"]])
```

```{r a2-observed-table}
observed <- data.frame(
  School = unname(school_labels[schools$entity_id]),
  `CDS identifier` = schools$entity_id,
  `Chronic-absence count` = schools$chronic_absent_count,
  `Eligible count` = schools$eligible_count,
  `Observed rate (%)` = round(100 * schools$observed_rate, 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(observed, row.names = FALSE)
```

Each school's count `y` is modeled as $\mathrm{Binomial}(n, p)$ given its
latent chronic-absence probability `p`. A piecewise-uniform empirical-Bayes
prior `G` over `161` continuous bins was estimated once on the full
`5,834`-school frame (with roughness penalty `lambda = 10`, a prior-fitting
parameter distinct from the unordered-pair cost `tau` below) and held fixed
for these 12 schools rather than refitted to the 12-school subset. Given `G`
and `(y, n)`, a school's posterior within each bin is a truncated
`Beta(y + 1, n - y + 1)` density weighted by its posterior bin mass. All
means, 90% intervals, and pairwise probabilities integrate that continuous
density; uncertainty in estimating `G` itself is held fixed and not
propagated.

## Priority direction and reporting loss {#orient-the-criterion-and-choose-the-report}

Because `postrank()` gives higher priority to larger target values, the target
is defined as $\theta = -p$ so lower chronic-absence probabilities receive
grade 1, and placing school `i` above school `j` reports $p_i < p_j$
($\theta_i > \theta_j$). Under the continuous piecewise-Beta posterior, two
schools have zero probability of exact equality, and placing them in the same
grade leaves their comparison unordered without claiming equal absence rates.

The analysis allows at most `G_max = 3` grades and prices each unordered pair
at `tau = 0.20`, relative to cost `1` for a wrong-direction ordered pair. Over
all `M` unordered pairs, a grading that orders `N` pairs with total posterior
expected wrong-direction errors `E` has loss
`R = (E + tau * (M - N)) / M`. With one criterion, `weights` defaults to `1`.

Recomputing the grading requires a solver (Gurobi is the default and needs a
license; `backend = "highs"` uses the open-source `highs` package from
`install.packages("highs")`). The solver call is shown below with
`eval = FALSE`, and the stored result from an equivalent call is loaded with
`postrank_example()`:

```{r a2-optional-solve, eval=FALSE}
analysis <- postrank(
  input,
  tau = 0.20, G_max = 3L,
  level = 0.90,
  backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 30, threads = 1L, seed = 1304L),
  fragility = FALSE
)
```

```{r a2-load-analysis}
analysis <- postrank_example("case_cde_12")
analysis
```

In the console output, "disclosed" means ordered pairs and "withheld" means
unordered pairs.

## Grades, report card, and expected error profile {#read-the-chosen-grades-and-their-uncertainty}

The stored grading uses `3` grades (`3 / 6 / 3` schools):

```{r a2-grade-table}
grades <- get_grades(analysis)
grade_groups <- lapply(sort(unique(grades)), function(g) {
  ids <- names(grades)[grades == g]
  data.frame(Grade = g, Schools = length(ids),
    Members = paste(unname(school_labels[ids]), collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, grade_groups), row.names = FALSE)
```

`postrank_plot_report_card()` plots the posterior means and 90% equal-tail
marginal intervals for $\theta = -p$ within each assigned grade, ordered by
posterior mean:

```{r a2-card, fig.height=5.8, fig.cap="Posterior means and 90% equal-tail marginal intervals for theta = -p across the 12 selected California schools, grouped by assigned grade.", fig.alt="Horizontal dot-and-interval report card for 12 schools (School A through School L) on theta = -p across grades 1 (3 schools), 2 (6 schools), and 3 (3 schools)."}
postrank_plot_report_card(
  analysis, order = "mean", order_by = input$criterion_ids,
  max_rows = nrow(schools), ncol = 1L,
  entity_labels = school_labels, criterion_labels = criterion_labels
)
```

Values closer to `0` correspond to lower chronic-absence probabilities. On
the negated scale, each school's mean is $-E[p]$ and its 90% marginal interval
is $[-q_{0.95}(p), -q_{0.05}(p)]$ (taken one school at a time rather than
simultaneously across all 12 schools). Because `input` stores only those 90%
endpoints, pass `level = 0.90`; other interval levels cannot be computed from
`input` alone.

```{r a2-profile}
profile <- get_profile(analysis)
profile[, c("criterion", "E", "E_over_N", "E_over_M", "risk")]
get_risk(analysis)
```

Out of `M = 66` unordered school pairs, the grading orders `N = 45` (`68.2%`)
and leaves `21` pairs unordered. Its posterior expected wrong-direction count
is `E = 0.00911`, or `0.020%` (`0.000203`) per ordered pair (`0.014%` across
all `66` pairs). Total loss is `0.063774`, of which `0.063636`
(`0.20 * 21 / 66`) comes from the `21` unordered pairs and `0.000138` from
expected wrong-direction errors. The solver finished with status `"optimal"`,
lower bound `0.063774`, and gap `1.39e-17` (which measures optimization over
the supplied probability matrix rather than quadrature or model error).

## Pairwise support inside the middle grade {#a-withheld-pair-can-still-have-a-clear-direction}

`postrank_plot_relations()` shows the `45` ordered pairs (colored cells) and
`21` unordered pairs (gray cells) in one upper triangle:

```{r a2-relations, fig.height=5.4, fig.cap="Pairwise ordering decisions across the 12 California schools, with ordered pairs in color and unordered within-grade pairs in gray.", fig.alt="Upper-triangular matrix for Schools A through L showing 45 ordered pairs between grades and 21 gray unordered pairs within grades 1, 2, and 3."}
postrank_plot_relations(analysis, entity_labels = school_labels)
```

Grade 2 holds `6` schools (`Schools D` through `I`). Plotting their pairwise
directional-error probabilities $\Pr(\theta_i \le \theta_j)$ illustrates why
leaving a pair unordered is different from finding the two schools similar:

```{r a2-middle-pairwise, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Posterior directional-error probabilities Pr(theta_i <= theta_j) among the six schools in grade 2.", fig.alt="Six-by-six heatmap of directional-error probabilities for Schools D through I inside grade 2, including near-zero error cells such as School F above School I."}
middle_ids <- names(grades)[grades == 2L]
postrank_plot_pairwise(
  analysis, entities = middle_ids, ncol = 1L,
  entity_labels = school_labels, criterion_labels = criterion_labels
)
```

Inside grade 2, the posterior probability that `School F` has lower chronic
absence than `School I` is `99.99%` (`0.999896`), yet their comparison is left
unordered because `G_max = 3` allows at most three grades across all 12
schools: splitting `School F` from `School I` would shift grade boundaries for
other pairs as well.

## Evaluating fixed tertile and all-unordered reports {#compare-reports-under-the-same-choices}

Using `postrank_evaluate()`, we evaluate three fixed alternatives on the same
12 schools, posterior probabilities, and `tau = 0.20` without running a
solver: leaving all pairs unordered, fixed observed-rate tertiles (`4 / 4 / 4`),
and fixed posterior-mean tertiles (`4 / 4 / 4`):

```{r a2-fixed-actions}
fixed <- lapply(case$reference$actions, function(g) {
  postrank_evaluate(g, input, weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = 0.20)
})
evaluations <- c(list(optimized = analysis$evaluation), fixed)
method_names <- c(
  optimized = "Optimized grades (3 / 6 / 3)",
  all_withheld = "All pairs unordered (12)",
  observed_rate_tertiles = "Observed-rate tertiles (4 / 4 / 4)",
  posterior_mean_tertiles = "Posterior-mean tertiles (4 / 4 / 4)"
)
comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(m) {
  z <- evaluations[[m]]
  data.frame(
    Report = unname(method_names[m]),
    `Ordered pairs` = z$N,
    `Expected errors` = round(unname(z$E), 4),
    `Errors / N (%)` = if (z$N == 0L) "NA" else as.character(round(100 * unname(z$E_over_N), 3)),
    Loss = round(z$primary_risk, 6),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
```

In this 12-school subset, observed-rate tertiles and posterior-mean tertiles
assign the same grades, ordering `48` pairs (`3` more than the optimized
grading) with `E = 1.8288` expected wrong-direction errors (`3.810%` per
ordered pair) and loss `0.082255` versus `0.063774`. Leaving all pairs
unordered gives loss `tau = 0.200000` and `Errors / N = NA` because `N = 0`.
This comparison applies to these 12 schools and settings and does not claim
that one procedure dominates score-cut rules in general.

## Relation to the 5,834-school statewide analysis {#relate-the-example-to-the-statewide-study}

`case$reference$statewide$metrics` stores summary rows from the separate
statewide analysis of all `5,834` eligible schools (`17,014,861` pairs) at
`tau = 0.20` and `G_max = 3`. Those statewide baselines sort schools by a
chosen score and optimize contiguous grade cutpoints along that fixed order
(rather than solving an unrestricted 5,834-school integer program):

```{r a2-statewide-table}
state <- case$reference$statewide$metrics
keep <- c("posterior_mean", "raw_rate", "expected_rank", "all_tie")
state_show <- state[match(keep, state$method), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Method = c("Posterior-mean cuts", "Observed-rate cuts",
    "Expected-rank cuts", "All pairs unordered"),
  `Ordered pairs` = format(state_show$N, big.mark = ","),
  `Ordered (%)` = round(100 * state_show$N_over_M, 1),
  `Errors / N (%)` = ifelse(state_show$N == 0L, "NA",
    as.character(round(100 * state_show$E_over_N, 2))),
  Loss = round(state_show$risk, 6),
  check.names = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

With optimal contiguous cuts of the posterior-mean ordering, the statewide
report orders `66.7%` of pairs with `1.32%` expected errors per ordered pair and
loss `0.075487` (versus `0.075479` for expected-rank cuts, illustrating that
posterior-mean ordering need not minimize loss even on one criterion). An
independent-pair relaxation gives lower bound `0.067091` (relaxation gap
`0.008396`), which compares fixed-order cuts against a pair-by-pair relaxation
rather than solving the unrestricted statewide problem.

Finally, `case$reference$quadrature$checks` records numerical quadrature checks
on the 12-school input across `16`, `32`, and `64` Gauss-Legendre nodes per
prior bin: the largest successive-order probability difference is `2.22e-15`,
and symmetric complement adjustment at `16` nodes changed entries by at most
`7.77e-16`. Those checks confirm quadrature stability; they do not verify the
binomial empirical-Bayes model or bound integration error outside the tested
orders.

This teaching dataset accompanies JoonHo Lee (2026), *How Much Can School
Accountability Indicators Distinguish? Uncertainty-Aware Reporting of Chronic
Absenteeism and Suspension in California*; full preparation records live in
`pr_case_cde$provenance` and `pr_case_cde$reference`.
